visual.general_description: Grayscale axial head MRI slice at the level of the orbits and skull base.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale axial MRI slice through both orbits. Both globes appear as rounded dark (low-signal) structures anteriorly, surrounded by brighter orbital fat, and a thin grey band (optic nerve) runs backward from each globe within the bright orbital fat toward the orbital apex. Between the orbits is a dark, air-filled nasal/ethmoid region with fine septa. Posteriorly lie the temporal lobes on either side, the dark-grey pons with a small dark fourth-ventricle/cistern opening, and the cerebellar hemispheres; scalp and facial soft tissue form a bright rim with both ears at the lateral edges. Two small yellow text labels are burned into the image: "AFR" at top centre and "PHL" at bottom centre. No arrows, panel letters, left/right side markers, scale bar or measurements are present. The image is grayscale, so no colour overlay or enhancement map is visible, and the slice does not by itself show whether contrast was given.

pixel_observations: Single grayscale axial MRI slice, 669 x 654 pixels, with the orbits at the top and the cerebellum at the bottom of the frame.
Both globes are dark rounded structures within bright orbital fat; a thin grey linear optic nerve is visible behind each globe in the orbit on both sides.
The paranasal/ethmoid region between the orbits is dark with thin septa; temporal lobes flank the midline, with pons and cerebellar hemispheres posteriorly.
Yellow text "AFR" at top centre and "PHL" at bottom centre; no side (left/right) marker, arrow, panel label, scale or numeric annotation.
Scalp, facial soft tissue and both ears are included at the image edges; the slice level is through the orbits so the eyes and part of the face are in frame.

clinical_significance.statement: Absence of new enhancing lesions plus infection led the authors to adjudicate the episode as a pseudo-relapse rather than an NMOSD relapse.

evidence.quote: In this case, the absence of new enhancing lesions and the presence of infection led to adjudication as a pseudo-relapse.

limitations: No left/right marker is visible, so which orbit is the left (atrophic) one cannot be determined from the image.
Optic nerve calibre, enhancement and atrophy were not independently assessed from this single compressed slice; findings rest on the caption.
A single grayscale slice cannot show whether contrast was administered; "post-contrast" and "T1-weighted" come from the caption.
The meaning of the yellow "AFR" and "PHL" text is not stated in the article and is not interpreted.
Whole figure is one unlettered image; analysis limited to what is visible at 669 x 654 pixels.

assignments.subject: patient

evidence.quote: An MRI of the brain, orbits and spine with contrast showed no new lesions or optic nerve enhancement; however, it demonstrated left optic nerve atrophy, without evidence of acute demyelination (Fig. 1).

Fig. 1.
Axial T1-weighted post-contrast orbital MRI showing bilateral absence of optic nerve enhancement, consistent with the absence of active optic neuritis. Left optic nerve atrophy is evident.

assignments.rationale: The index-patient MRI sentence calls out Fig. 1 and the caption describes the same absence of enhancement and left optic nerve atrophy; the case has one patient. No identity is inferred from the image.
